column4: Guards swinging a gate shut were invented; the captain of the guard only puts the two officers in Joseph's charge (40:3-4).
Joseph carried an invented water jar (40:6-7).
Showed a vineyard and Pharaoh on a throne; the dream has one vine with three branches, and the cup given into Pharaoh's hand (40:9-11).
Left out the baker, who hears this interpretation (40:16); added other prisoners and a midday light, though Joseph came to them in the morning (40:6).
Invented a road across a plain, a flock of black birds and the baker failing to drive them off; the text has birds eating from the top basket (40:16-17).
Removed a golden cup, music and dusk, which the text doesn't give (40:20-21).
Removed 'at dawn', a time the text doesn't give; the lean kine now stand by the fat ones on the brink of the river (41:3).
Showed a vast field and Pharaoh under a midday sun; the dream has one stalk with seven ears and seven thin ears after them (41:5-6).
Moved to a palace terrace, Joseph pointing over the valley at dust on the horizon; he is still speaking before Pharaoh in the hall (41:25-32).
Joseph scooping wheat from a basket and the late-afternoon shadows were invented; he only counsels Pharaoh (41:33-36).
Pharaoh coming down the steps, the evening sun and a light falling on Joseph were invented (41:37-40).
Removed the avenue of sphinxes and Pharaoh watching from the palace gate, which the text doesn't give (41:42-43).
Set at the temple of On among obelisks with Poti-pherah present, none of which the text gives (41:45); Asenath now has a cast key.
Joseph standing in his chariot was invented; he gathers the food into the cities (41:48).
Joseph lifting the baby to the sky, servants lighting lamps and the dusk were invented; the text gives only the two births and their names (41:50-52).
Pharaoh was high on a balcony and the Nile shrunken, neither in the text; the people cry to Pharaoh, who sends them to Joseph (41:55).
Jacob was the key for his prime; he is nearly a hundred and thirty (47:9), so Jacob (old). Dropped the dawn the text doesn't give.
Guards with spears closing in and the noon sun were invented (42:9-16).
Guards behind Joseph and 'the third morning' are not in the text, which says only 'the third day' (42:17-18).
Split 42:21-24: Simeon was bound after Joseph turned away to weep (42:24). Here the brothers confess and Reuben speaks; Joseph listens, with his interpreter (42:23).
Split 42:21-24. Guards bound Simeon while Joseph wept, but Joseph wept first, then 'took from them Simeon, and bound him before their eyes' (42:24).
Silver put into the sacks and the brothers leaving were shown at once, though the silver was put in unknown to them (42:25, 42:27-28).
A campfire under a starry night was invented; the text has only 'the inn', a lodging place on the way (42:27).
Jacob was the key for his prime; he is nearly a hundred and thirty (47:9), so Jacob (old).
Jacob was the key for his prime; he is nearly a hundred and thirty (47:9). Dropped the lamplit evening the text doesn't give.
Jacob was the key for his prime; he is nearly a hundred and thirty (47:9), so Jacob (old).
Jacob was the key for his prime; he is nearly a hundred and thirty (47:9). Dropped the sunset the text doesn't give.
Jacob was the key for his prime (47:9); dawn dropped; the present is 'a little' of each thing (43:11).
A servant led Simeon out; the steward himself 'brought Simeon out unto them' (43:23).
Servants bringing basins and a splashing fountain were invented; the steward 'gave them water' (43:24).
A servant holding a towel was invented, and the brothers seen through the door; Joseph weeps alone in his chamber (43:30-31).
Lit by lamps, but the meal was at noon (43:16, 43:25).
Joseph handing over the cup and the steward hiding it were shown at once; now Joseph gives the command (44:1-2). Dropped the moonlit courtyard.
Horsemen galloping with the steward were invented; the text has the steward following the men and overtaking them (44:4, 44:6).
The steward was mounted, with horsemen, which the text doesn't give (44:6-10).
The harsh midday sun doesn't fit: they left at first light and were 'not yet far off' (44:3-4).
Joseph holding the cup and a guard at Benjamin's side were invented, and the afternoon time (44:14-17).
Benjamin stood between two guards, which the text doesn't give (44:18-23).
Evening light doesn't fit: the brothers left at first light and were brought back the same morning (44:3-13).
Servants lighting lamps at dusk doesn't fit the morning of the brothers' return (44:3-13).
Showed Egyptians still leaving, in a lamp-lit hall; 'there stood no man with him' while he made himself known (45:1), and it was day (44:3).
Moonlight is wrong: this is the day the brothers were brought back in the morning (44:3-13, 45:1).
Moved to a palace terrace at sunrise, Joseph pointing to Goshen; he speaks to them in the same room, the same day (45:1-13).
Set on a terrace above the city; they are still in the room where he made himself known (45:1-15).
Wagons being readied with oxen were invented; Pharaoh only commands that wagons be taken (45:19, 45:21).
Dropped the dawn the text doesn't give; the she-asses carry meat as well as corn and bread (45:23).
Jacob swaying, steadied by Benjamin, then lifting his staff toward Egypt were invented, and the sunset; his spirit revives at the sight of the wagons (45:26-27).
Gave a count of thirty-three for a group that also holds the wives the count leaves out (46:15, 46:26); now no number.
Children chasing one another round fires at a palm oasis under the stars were invented; now a plain camp with Benjamin's ten sons (46:21).
Removed the green delta and the sunset: five years of famine were still to come (45:6, 47:13), and the text gives no time of day.
Had the two weeping on each other's necks; the text has Joseph weeping on his father's neck (46:29). The gilded chariot and bright morning were invented.
Pharaoh rising from his throne and the golden evening light were invented (47:7-10).
Showed lush green fields while the famine was still 'very sore' (47:13); now pasture for the flocks.
The courtiers' key dressed the hungry farmers as officials; they are now described as farmers (47:15-17).
Joseph in his chariot and priests standing by their temple were invented staging (47:18-22).
Families already sowing in rows came before their time; Joseph gives the seed and tells them to sow (47:23-25).
Jacob gripping Joseph's hand stood in for the oath; now the moment after it, as Israel 'bowed himself upon the bed's head' (47:31).
Servants helped Jacob sit up, but 'Israel strengthened himself, and sat upon the bed' (48:2). By the numbers Joseph's sons are twenty or more (41:46-50, 47:28).
The household watching from the doorway was invented, and the embrace and Joseph's bowing to the earth were shown at once (48:10-12).
Servants looking on from the doorway were invented (48:17-20).
The weather turned cold and overcast in the middle of the one gathering (49:1-2); kept the same room and light.
Showed a great lion; Judah is 'a lion's whelp' (49:9). Kept the sceptre and the foal tied to the vine (49:10-11); dropped the sunrise and the bowing crowd.
Fishermen hauling nets and farmers bent under burdens were invented; Jacob's words have a haven of ships and a strong ass between two burdens (49:13-15).
A judge at a town gate and an evening star 'as if waiting for deliverance' were invented; kept the adder, the horse's heels and the falling rider (49:16-18).
The landscape added a village with ovens and fleeing raiders to Jacob's words; now Jacob blessing Gad, Asher and Naphtali at his bed (49:1-2, 49:19-21).
Added archers lowering their bows and Joseph under the vine, beyond Jacob's words; kept the fruitful bough by a well, its branches over the wall, and the hills (49:22, 49:26).
Jacob laying his hand on Benjamin and a soft rain were invented (49:27-28). Benjamin, forty or more by now, no longer has the young man's key.
Physicians with spices and a crowd of mourners were shown with Joseph's first grief; the embalming and Egypt's mourning came after (50:2-3). Dropped the grey before dawn.
Joseph asked Pharaoh at the throne; he spoke to 'the house of Pharaoh', asking them to speak 'in the ears of Pharaoh' (50:4).
Showed a coffin; the text gives one only for Joseph (50:26). His sons carried him (50:13); the little ones and flocks stayed in Goshen (50:8).
Showed a coffin, sackcloth and a hilltop threshing floor, none of them in the text (50:10-11).
Showed a coffin, oaks and olive trees, and Joseph leading; 'his sons carried him' (50:13), with no coffin named. Dropped the waiting chariots.
The messenger waiting by the gate was invented; the brothers sent him first and then came themselves (50:16-18).
Their children watching and Judah singled out were invented (50:19-21).
Parents gathered smiling were added; kept Joseph and the little children brought up upon his knees (50:23).
A coffin waited before his death, at dusk; it comes after he died (50:26). His brethren are shown as old men, not with the younger brothers' key.
